verdict.headline: Palantir crushes earnings with Pentagon AI windfall as US factories hit a four-year high
verdict.label: BUY — 2 of 6 breached (30Y 5.23%, WTI $80.01); PLTR +15% AH on Q2 blowout ($1.94B rev vs $1.81B est, +93% YoY, EPS $0.41 vs $0.35; FY26 guidance raised $500M to $8.15B); ISM Mfg 55.6 (est. 54.0, 7th consecutive expansion month, prices paid 71.1 ↓ from 73.0); Sept hike ~55% Polymarket (below 70% trigger); SPX futures +0.21% to ~7,557; AMD and SpaceX (SPCX) first earnings AH tonight; JOLTS 10 AM ET; NFP Fri Aug 7
verdict.rationale_short: The week's largest binary resolved overnight: PLTR Q2 revenue of $1.94B (+93% YoY) beat consensus by $123M, EPS of $0.41 beat by 18.5%, and management raised FY26 guidance by nearly $500M to $8.15–$8.16B — 82% implied full-year growth. US Government revenue of $809M grew +90% YoY and US Commercial boomed +149% YoY. The DoD AI urgency thesis is not a narrative; it is a compounding revenue line that now arrives audited. PLTR stock is +15% AH to ~$144.45, above the $140+ beat target from Monday's setup, and the print simultaneously validates AMZN's $25B+ AI revenue run rate (July 31) and sets a high bar for AMD's data-center GPU print tonight. ISM Manufacturing adds a second pillar: July headline 55.6 (est. 54.0), highest since May 2022, seventh consecutive month of expansion. Prices paid eased to 71.1 from 73.0 — third consecutive monthly moderation — while Employment broke into expansion for the first time in 33 months. This is the Goldilocks configuration for equities: strong factory activity confirming tariff-rerouting growth without accelerating input cost inflation. September hike probability continues declining: 82.4% (Aug 1) → 63% (Aug 3) → ~55% today (Polymarket), a 27-point three-session collapse, clearing the 70% formal trigger by a widening margin. Regime holds at 2 of 6 breached: 30Y at 5.229% remains the structural durable breach; WTI at $80.01 ($1.01 above the $79 trigger) is the softest remaining breach, with Monday's intraday low of $78.26 proving bid support and OPEC+ September supply increase sustaining downward pressure. BTC $63,794.53 (+1.68%, Crypto.com MCP 11:01 UTC) has restored the Gate 2 buffer to $1,794 from Monday's $680 — PLTR's government revenue beat removes the fastest path to a $62,000 test. SPX futures +0.21% (~7,557), Nasdaq +0.60%; DXY ~99.97 (flat); 10Y at 4.67% (−4bps). Tonight's remaining risk events: AMD Q2 AH (consensus $11.3B revenue, EPS $1.61; Helios rack-system orders and gross margin in the mid-50s are the key signals beyond the headline) and SpaceX (SPCX) first-ever public earnings AH (est. $6.9B revenue, +68% YoY; stock down 45%+ from June IPO high at $225.64 — any Starlink profitability confirmation or xAI monetization path restores a portion of the premium). JOLTS June at 10 AM ET (prior May reading: 7.594M, well above 7.30M est.) is the morning's labor-market probe. If SPX closes below 7,380 or AMD prints a data-center revenue deceleration that cascades into NVDA sell-side revisions, this read no longer holds.

trade_setups.thesis: AMD reports Q2 after the close tonight. Consensus: $11.3B revenue, EPS $1.61. PLTR's government revenue blowout (+90% YoY) and commercial AI acceleration (+149%) provide the strongest AI demand read-through since AMZN AWS. AMD's binary is specifically about data-center GPU revenue (MI350 shipments vs. prior MI300 mix), the pace of Helios rack-scale system orders, and Q3 guidance vs. the Street. A confirmed Helios backlog comparable to NVDA's Blackwell disclosure cadence would validate a multi-quarter forward revenue line. Gross margin in the mid-50s is the structural signal that the Helios cost ramp is on schedule. A soft Q3 guide or gross margin sliding toward low-50s signals execution risk and removes the PLTR-driven read-through.
trade_setups.entry: Risk-defined exposure into tonight's close. $480-500 is the clean-beat, clean-guide resistance; $410-420 is the post-miss support zone. Options pricing ~8-10% swing.
trade_setups.invalidation: Soft Q3 guide, below-consensus data-center GPU revenue, or gross margin below mid-50s removes the Helios ramp thesis and creates a negative read-through to NVDA.

trade_setups.thesis: SpaceX reports first-ever public quarterly earnings AH tonight. Stock IPO'd at $135 on June 11, hit $225.64 on June 16, now down 45%+ to ~$120. Revenue estimate $6.9B (+68% YoY). First audited financials for a company that raised $85.7B in the largest IPO in history — valuation discovery event. Q1 showed a $4.28B net loss on $4.69B revenue, implying ongoing heavy capex burn. Starlink profitability (unit economics at scale, subscriber count) and xAI revenue recognition are the two numbers the market has never seen in audited form. A confirmed Starlink EBITDA-positive segment + xAI monetization path could close much of the gap from $120 toward the $225 high.
trade_setups.entry: Post-print reaction is cleaner than pre-print at this uncertainty level. At ~$120 the stock already prices elevated uncertainty; a confirmed Starlink profitability inflection is a re-rating catalyst; continued large net losses on missed revenue revisits the IPO price ($135) or below.
trade_setups.invalidation: Q2 net loss exceeding $5B on $6.9B revenue, Starlink subscriber deceleration, or xAI capex disclosure without a monetization timeline confirms the burn-rate risk at current pricing.

trade_setups.asset: JOLTS June 2026 — labor regime check at 10 AM ET
trade_setups.thesis: JOLTS June 2026 releases at 10:00 AM ET. Prior May reading: 7.594M (beat 7.30M est., highest since May 2024). Today's reading matters for two reasons: (1) ISM Employment broke into expansion for the first time in 33 months this morning — a JOLTS print above 7.5M confirms a tightening labor market and could nudge September hike odds from ~55% back toward 60-65%; (2) the prior 7.594M reading was already inconsistent with the sub-200K NFP consensus for Friday Aug 7. A hot JOLTS adds upward pressure to 30Y yield and potentially reinstates rate-path risk that Monday's Iran peace narrative removed.
trade_setups.entry: Watch 10Y yield within 15 minutes of 10:00 AM ET: drop below 4.60% on a JOLTS miss confirms disinflationary track and widens clearance from the hike trigger; rise above 4.75% on a hot print reverses morning rate-relief and complicates the BUY call.
trade_setups.invalidation: JOLTS above 7.8M with ISM at 55.6 and Employment in expansion is a labor-market tightening triple: would push September hike odds above 65% and pressure 30Y toward 5.35%.

bear_case: The 2-of-6 regime count is unchanged from Monday, and the morning's apparent bullishness rests substantially on a single PLTR print. ISM Manufacturing at 55.6 is the highest since May 2022 — this is a hot reading, not Goldilocks. Prices paid at 71.1 remains above 70 for six consecutive months: a sustained inflationary signal the FOMC explicitly tracks and that contributed three dissenting votes for an immediate hike at the July 29 meeting. Employment breaking into expansion for the first time in 33 months directly undercuts the sub-200K NFP consensus for Friday Aug 7; if JOLTS at 10 AM ET today shows job openings above 7.8M, September hike probability can rebound from 55% back above 65-70% in a single session, reinstating that formal breach and negating two of the three regime improvements since Monday. AMD tonight at ~$430-450 is its own binary: if data-center GPU revenue disappoints or gross margin slides toward the low-50s, the read-through to NVDA is negative and the AI capex narrative (the primary SPX multiple-expander since May) comes under direct pressure — the PLTR-driven read-through cuts both ways. SpaceX first earnings are a pure discovery event; the $4.28B Q1 net loss on $4.69B revenue suggests continued heavy burn, and if Q2 losses exceed $5B on $6.9B revenue without a Starlink profitability anchor, the IPO premium structurally evaporates. WTI at $80.01 is $1.01 above the $79 formal trigger; any Iran re-escalation, pipeline disruption, or OPEC+ signal revision closes that gap in one session and simultaneously reinstates the Brent breach near $85. The 30Y at 5.229% has been above 5.00% for over a month without a structural break; clearing it requires cooling NFP (Friday) combined with sub-50 ISM Services (Wednesday). The morning's gap-up prices PLTR, ISM, JOLTS, AMD, and SpaceX all resolving cleanly and without feedback-loop implications on each other. Any one disappointment resets the 2-of-6 picture toward 3-of-6.
